title: a combined request+response body over the 2 MiB transport cap is rejected as 400
specRef: lib/http.js:17 MAX_BODY_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024 documents the per-request transport cap; readJson() rejects a body once it exceeds this limit with code payload_too_large before Core validation ever runs (modules/analyze/handler.js:390 maps every readJson() rejection to HTTP 400).
specNotes: The posted body is 2106113 bytes, 8961 bytes over the 2097152-byte cap; the response side is the base pair's own small response, unchanged, so the overage comes entirely from request.ext.pad.

This case asserts only the HTTP transport contract. Core is not applicable here (the payload is rejected before parsing reaches validate()) and is intentionally left with no request/response/crosscheck expectations — tests/corpus-core.test.js skips it via coreApplicability() and asserts that knownGap does not name the core layer.

The body-cap contract requires the documented HTTP 400 payload_too_large envelope. Actual connection reset is recorded as status 0 with the transport cause, never as an HTTP response. Exact DEF-303 signatures admit only the reproduced reset and missing envelope; timeouts or other failures remain unexpected.
